question.text: In a potentiometer arrangement, a cell gives a balancing point at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>75</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> length of wire. This cell is now replaced by another cell of unknown emf. If the ratio of the emf's of two cells respectively is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo>:</mo><mn>2</mn></math>, the difference in the balancing length of the potentiometer wire in above two cases will be _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>cm</mi></math>.

solution.text:
If the potential difference between the potentiometer is V and the potential of the battery is ε. 

Then, εV=lL

Therefore, ε1ε2=l1l2⇒32=75x⇒x=50 cm

Therefore, the difference in the balancing length is 75-50=25 cm
